current_example.problem: Given that $\dfrac{x}{3} + 2y = 1,$ express $x$ in terms of $y.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ To do this, we treat $y$ as though it were a constant and apply the addition and multiplication principles as usual.

First, we subtract $2y$ from both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3}+2y & =1 \\ \frac{x}{3}+2y-2y & =1-2y \\ \frac{x}{3}+0 & =1-2y \\ \frac{x}{3} & =1-2y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we multiply both sides of the equation by $3\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{3} & =1-2y \\ 3\cdot \frac{x}{3} & =3\cdot (1-2y) \\ \cancel{3}\cdot \frac{x}{\cancel{3}} & =3\cdot (1-2y) \\ x & =3\cdot (1-2y) \\ x & =3\cdot 1-3\cdot 2y \\ x & =3-6y\end{aligned}
$$
